Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Liam Nguyen (Redwood SE), James Ellis (SilverGrove CTO), Maria Lopez (Head of ML), Tom Rhee (Infra Lead), Angela Park (Security)
summary: Discovery focused on dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools, isolation/VPC requirements, burst/burst-to-hosted strategy, autoscaling expectations, and compliance needs. Customer is evaluating dedicated vs hosted for production due to data sensitivity and predictable throughput requirements. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing, security packet, and benchmark plan; customer to share traffic traces and compliance checklist.
topics: Security and compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account, we've got Priya and Liam from the SE team. Quick intro?
[00:10] James Ellis: James here, CTO at SilverGrove. Maria is our head of ML, Tom infra, Angela security.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Great, thanks. Goal for today is to understand your workload shape and constraints so we can size a Dedicated offering — reserved GPUs, isolation, burst patterns, and compliance checks.
[00:29] Maria Lopez: Right, high level: we run a customer support assistant and a risk-detection pipeline. The assistant is low-latency interactive, risk pipeline is batch-ish but needs to scale in peaks. Data is sensitive — PII plus financial transaction metadata.
[00:44] Tom Rhee: We're leaning to Dedicated because we need network isolation and auditability. We might also want a private deployment later but start with Dedicated.
[00:53] Alex Kim: Makes sense. Can you share what you run today? Cloud? GPUs?
[01:00] James Ellis: We're on AWS, EC2 instances with a mix of RTX 6000 and some older A10s. For model hosting we currently use in-house endpoints for a finetuned Llama-2 variant, we've hit scaling pain — cold starts and variable latency at peak.
[01:18] Priya Rao: Thanks. A couple questions: typical QPS for the assistant, average and 95th pct latency targets, and sequence lengths?
[01:27] Maria Lopez: Assistant avg QPS is around 12 qps, 95th ~45 during promos. Latency target is user-facing <350ms for short prompts (~128 tokens). Risk pipeline spikes to ~300 concurrent jobs, not latency-sensitive but throughput sensitive. Sequence lengths vary — many short prompts (40-200 tokens) and some long risk queries up to 2k tokens.
[01:51] Liam Nguyen: For Dedicated we normally recommend reserving capacity for your baseline and enabling burst to Hosted for spikes, or configuring burst capacity within Dedicated if you commit to larger GPU pools. Do you have an ops preference?
[02:03] Tom Rhee: Prefer burst to Hosted as fallback — we want isolation for steady state but willing to accept spillover in overload, as long as data residency and encryption guarantees hold.
[02:13] Angela Park: On the security side we need SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML, KMS integration (customer-managed keys), audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and the ability to pin models — we cannot have unknown model versions serving PII.
[02:28] Priya Rao: All standard. Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and private connectivity, KMS/HSM integrations, and model version pinning. Audit logs and token-level tracing can be exported to your SIEM. We'll include our security packet.
[02:42] James Ellis: Questions around autoscaling — we need predictable throughput for business SLAs. How do you handle autoscale and cold-starts?
[02:50] Priya Rao: Our runtime uses continuous batching and a warm pool. For Dedicated we can configure a minimum warm pool sized to ensure latency SLOs; autoscale policies can be based on queue depth or latency. Cold-starts are minimized — we do pre-warming and keep a minimum of GPU instances allocated. For spikes we can either allow burst to Hosted or pre-configure dedicated burst buffers.
[03:12] Maria Lopez: For risk jobs with long seq lengths, memory and KV cache are big — how do you size for that?
[03:18] Liam Nguyen: We look at sequence length distribution, model memory footprint (FP16 vs quantized), and KV cache growth. For long sequences you either need larger GPUs with more memory or run model parallelism. We'll propose a mix — some larger-memory GPUs for the 2k token runs and more numerous smaller GPUs for the assistant.
[03:38] Tom Rhee: Cost-wise, what's the tradeoff between committing to larger dedicated pool versus more bursts to Hosted?
[03:44] Alex Kim: Committing buys predictability and better unit cost; bursts to Hosted give flexibility and lower up-front commits but variance in latency and potential additional egress or routing costs. We can model expected unit economics if you share trace data.
[03:58] Angela Park: Regarding data in transit to Hosted during burst: does PII cross Redwood-managed multi-tenant systems? We need assurance of encryption and no persistent logs.
[04:09] Priya Rao: During burst to Hosted we can use encrypted in-transit and in-use protections. However, if your policy forbids any multi-tenant handling of PII, then burst-to-hosted won't be acceptable. In that case Dedicated-only or a Private deployment is the option. We'll surface those constraints in the security packet.
[04:28] James Ellis: Good. Another operational question: maintenance windows and rollouts — we need canary and rollback capabilities.
[04:35] Liam Nguyen: Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B routing, and automatic fallbacks. You can pin routes to model versions and define automatic rollback policies if latency or quality regressions hit thresholds.
[04:47] Maria Lopez: We also need evaluation / quality monitoring — can we run evals against canary models automatically?
[04:52] Priya Rao: Yes, Redwood Optimize ties eval sets to deployments and can trigger alerts on quality regressions. We'll show examples in the follow-up deck.
[04:59] Alex Kim: To size the Dedicated environment, we'll need: traffic traces (QPS over time), sequence length distribution, model sizes, and acceptable latency SLOs. Tom, you mentioned sharing traces?
[05:08] Tom Rhee: Yes I'll get logs — probably a 7-14 day sample. Will that be enough?
[05:11] Priya Rao: That's ideal. Also include spike events and retention of failed requests.
[05:18] James Ellis: For burst capacity, are there SLA differences if we fall back to Hosted?
[05:24] Alex Kim: Hosted has a different SLA; for Dedicated we can contract for higher uptime/latency SLOs. If burst to Hosted, you get Hosted SLA for those requests — we'll clarify in the contract.
[05:36] Angela Park: On compliance, do you support customer-managed keys for encryption at rest?
[05:40] Priya Rao: Yes, KMS/HSM integrations are supported in Dedicated and Private. We'll include a diagram for key flow.
[05:47] Maria Lopez: Another thing: batch risk pipeline — can Redwood schedule and run that on Dedicated GPUs without impacting assistant latency?
[05:54] Liam Nguyen: You can isolate workloads via routing policies and queues. We recommend separate pools or prioritized queues — the runtime prioritizes low-latency traffic and shifts batch jobs to idle capacity. For sustained batch throughput, size separate pools.
[06:09] Tom Rhee: How about network isolation for outbound calls? We need egress control and whitelist only to our internal services.
[06:16] Priya Rao: VPC peering and egress restrictions are supported; you can route outbound through your network appliances. We'll include network topology examples.
[06:26] Alex Kim: Any blockers on procurement or timeline?
[06:29] James Ellis: Timeline: we plan a pilot in Q2, production in Q3. Procurement requires security signoff and pricing for a 12-month commitment.
[06:38] Angela Park: We'll need SOC2 package and contract language for data residency. Also a vendor security assessment — I'll send the questionnaire.
[06:44] Alex Kim: Perfect. We'll send the security packet and a proposed 12-month committed pricing. Priya will propose a benchmark plan.
[06:51] Maria Lopez: For the benchmark, we'll want to run both the assistant workload and a subset of long sequence risk jobs to validate latency and throughput.
[06:59] Priya Rao: Noted — we'll propose a 2-hour benchmark with warmup, steady-state, and spike phases.
[07:05] Liam Nguyen: One more note on model variants and quantization — if you want lowest cost per token, quantized models and gpus with optimized kernels help a lot, we'll recommend profiles.
[07:16] Maria Lopez: Are there restrictions on model uploads or custom containers?
[07:20] Priya Rao: Dedicated allows customer model artifacts with pinned versions. For Private you can run in your environment with more control; Dedicated supports private model storage and restricted access.
[07:31] James Ellis: OK let's recap. Action items?
[07:33] Alex Kim: Recap — Redwood to send pricing and security packet, SEs to share benchmark plan, customer to send traces and compliance checklist. We'll tentatively schedule the benchmark week of Mar 16.
[07:46] Tom Rhee: Sounds good. Anything else?
[07:48] Angela Park: No, we'll follow up via email with the security questionnaire.
[07:51] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday with the docs.
[07:55] James Ellis: Thanks, bye.
[07:57] (call ends)
